case: declaring an unanswered finding unpinnable, with a reason
why: The benign twin of r19-pin-citing-a-review-finding-deleted, moving the same control in the other direction. F6A-01 is one of the 37 findings this package declares a source for and says nothing about; adding an `unpinnable` row with a reason takes that set to 36, under the ceiling of 37. This must PASS: the ceiling exists to refuse a pin deletion, not to freeze the pin file, and the legitimate way to stop answering a finding -- say so, in writing, in the table a reviewer reads -- has to remain cheaper than the illegitimate one. A checker that refused this would be refusing every future declaration, which would teach an author to delete the finding_sources row instead and leave nothing behind at all. The `unpinnable` row alone is now HALF the edit: F6R-01's partition check reports 'declared but not unanswered' for a finding that is both unpinnable and in `not_answered`, so the benign edit this fixture models has to leave the partition consistent -- which is the partition doing its job on a fixture rather than on a repair. DRIFT REPAIR by lane r7-contracts-c: this benign fixture was FALSELY EXCLUDED on the merged head. It is the same class the package names elsewhere -- a fixture that encodes a snapshot of a table another lane then grew. The patch is regenerated from the current tree and the old shape is recorded here, because a benign fixture that fails looks exactly like a repair that broke something.
